# The Bhargava–Hanke 290 theorem in Lean 4

A positive-definite quadratic form with integer coefficients represents every positive integer if it represents 29 specified integers. This repository contains Chang Su's freely formalization of that criterion in Lean 4 and mathlib.

- [Read the five-page preprint (PDF)](https://zenodo.org/records/24570786/files/freely290-paper.pdf?download=1).
- [See the 29 integers and the exact theorem statement](https://github.com/vchangv520-lgtm/freely290/blob/v1.0.0/Freely290/Core.lean#L32-L49).
- [Open the two final Lean theorems](https://github.com/vchangv520-lgtm/freely290/blob/v1.0.0/Freely290/Completed290.lean#L8-L11).
- [Inspect the kernel result](https://github.com/vchangv520-lgtm/freely290/blob/v1.0.0/evidence/kernel-replay.log) or [replay the proof yourself](https://github.com/vchangv520-lgtm/freely290/blob/v1.0.0/README.md).

The source distribution contains 4,803 Lean files in the project proof closure. The verification report names both theorems and records the axioms, toolchain, dependency revision, and proof hash. [Verification report](https://github.com/vchangv520-lgtm/freely290/blob/v1.0.0/evidence/verified.json).

Cite the preprint and its accompanying proof as Chang Su, *A Lean 4 formalization of the Bhargava–Hanke 290 theorem*, version 1.0.0 (2026). [Zenodo DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24570786).
